_sources.usda: USDA FoodData Central, https://fdc.nal.usda.gov/ (record named in each entry), read 2026-10-27
_sources.nihOds: NIH Office of Dietary Supplements fact sheets (Iron, Folate, Vitamin C, Vitamin K, Magnesium, Zinc, Potassium, Vitamin A, Calcium, Vitamin B12, Vitamin D, Vitamin E), https://ods.od.nih.gov/factsheets/list-all/; reference intakes as listed in build_draft_batch.py (RDA for adult women)
_sources.niddk: NIDDK, Eating, Diet & Nutrition for Kidney Stones, read 2026-10-26: nuts and nut products, peanuts, rhubarb, spinach and wheat bran listed among foods to reduce for calcium oxalate stones

adzuki-bean.desc: Beans, adzuki, mature seeds, cooked, boiled, without salt
adzuki-bean.how: Simmer until soft, then use in rice dishes, soups, salads or sweetened bean paste.
adzuki-bean.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
adzuki-bean.reviewNote: USDA lists no vitamin E or K values for this record.
adzuki-bean.name: Adzuki bean

mung-bean.desc: Mung beans, mature seeds, cooked, boiled, without salt
mung-bean.how: Simmer until tender for dal, soups and porridge; whole mung beans cook faster than most beans.
mung-bean.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
mung-bean.reviewNote: Whole mung beans; sprouted mung beans have their own record.
mung-bean.name: Mung bean

great-northern-bean.desc: Beans, great northern, mature seeds, cooked, boiled, without salt
great-northern-bean.how: Soak, then simmer until creamy for soups, stews, casseroles and purees.
great-northern-bean.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
great-northern-bean.name: Great northern bean

navy-bean.desc: Beans, navy, mature seeds, cooked, boiled, without salt
navy-bean.how: Soak, then simmer for soups, stews and homemade baked beans.
navy-bean.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
navy-bean.name: Navy bean

baked-beans.desc: Beans, baked, canned, plain or vegetarian
baked-beans.how: Serve on toast, with eggs, or as a side; choose lower-sugar, lower-salt versions if you can.
baked-beans.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
baked-beans.reviewNote: Canned baked beans in sauce, which usually contains added sugar and salt (not shown in this nutrient set); varies by brand.
baked-beans.name: Baked beans

fava-beans.desc: Broadbeans (fava beans), mature seeds, cooked, boiled, without salt
fava-beans.how: Soak dried beans, then simmer for stews, dips and salads; peel the tough skins for a smoother texture.
fava-beans.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
fava-beans.reviewNote: Dried fava beans, cooked. Fresh young fava pods are a different food.
fava-beans.name: Fava (broad) beans

chestnut.how: Roast or boil and peel, then eat as is or add to stuffings, soups and purees.
chestnut.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
chestnut.reviewNote: Unlike most nuts, chestnuts are low in fat and high in starch. Raw, boiled and dried chestnuts differ; the record is roasted.
chestnut.name: Chestnut

hickory.how: Eat shelled nuts as a snack or chop into baking and porridge.
hickory.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
hickory.reviewNote: USDA lists no vitamin E or K values for this record.
hickory.name: Hickory

pine-nut.how: Toast lightly and scatter on salads and pasta, or blend into pesto.
pine-nut.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
pine-nut.reviewNote: Pine nuts as sold in shops. USDA's pinyon pine nut is a separate record.
pine-nut.name: Pine nut

hemp-seeds.how: Sprinkle over porridge, yoghurt, salads and smoothies.
hemp-seeds.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
hemp-seeds.reviewNote: Hulled hemp seed. Omega-3 and vitamin K are not given in this USDA record, so they are not shown.
hemp-seeds.name: Hemp seeds

macadamia-nuts.how: Eat a small handful, or chop into baking, granola and salads.
macadamia-nuts.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
macadamia-nuts.name: Macadamia nuts

tahini.desc: Seeds, sesame butter, tahini, type of kernels unspecified
tahini.how: Stir into dressings, hummus and sauces, or drizzle over roasted vegetables; stir the jar first as the oil separates.
tahini.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
tahini.reviewNote: USDA has several tahini records (roasted, raw, unroasted); the "kernels unspecified" one was chosen because the catalogue does not specify. Values differ between them, notably calcium.
tahini.name: Tahini

duck.desc: Duck, domesticated, meat only, cooked, roasted
duck.how: Roast or pan-sear, and remove the skin and extra fat if you want less fat.
duck.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
duck.reviewNote: Meat only without skin. Duck with skin has far more fat.
duck.name: Duck

bacon.how: Cook until crisp and use sparingly, for example crumbled over soups, salads and vegetables.
bacon.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
bacon.reviewNote: A cured, processed meat that is high in salt and fat (sodium is not shown here). No sourced caution was added beyond the catalogue's own.
bacon.name: Bacon

ham.desc: Pork, cured, ham, boneless, extra lean and regular, roasted
ham.how: Slice into sandwiches and salads, or dice into eggs, soups and pasta.
ham.evidence: Nutrient amounts and reference intakes only (USDA FoodData Central, NIH ODS).
ham.reviewNote: A cured, processed meat that is high in salt (sodium not shown here). Deli ham varies by brand.
ham.name: Ham
